title: Venting about working late
situation: A friend texts you at night complaining they're stuck at the office doing overtime again.
tip: When a friend vents, lead with a reaction (헐/진짜?) and a quick 되묻기 (왜?/언제 끝나?) so they feel heard — that's what keeps a venting chat alive.

turns.en: Ugh… I'm still at the office ㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask why they're still there.

choices.en: What, still?? Why are you working late again?
choices.feedback: 헐 (reaction) + 왜 또 야근해? (follow-up) is exactly how friends pick up a vent.

choices.en: Oh, you're still at the office. (formal)
choices.feedback: 계시는군요 is 존댓말 — way too formal for a friend venting.

choices.en: I'm kinda tired today too.
choices.feedback: Changes the subject to you instead of reacting to their complaint.

turns.ko: 내일까지 보고서 내야 돼서 ㅠㅠ 팀장이 갑자기 시킴
turns.en: I have to hand in a report by tomorrow ㅠㅠ my team lead just dumped it on me

turns.prompt: Sympathize and ask when they'll be done.

choices.en: Wow that's so unfair… when do you finish?
choices.feedback: Empathy (너무하다) plus 언제 끝나? keeps the conversation going and shows you care.

choices.en: Shall I help you write the report? (formal)
choices.feedback: 드릴까요 is 존댓말 — friends would say 도와줄까?, and it's a sudden offer that skips the empathy.

choices.en: Still, you get paid lol
choices.feedback: Dismissive — invalidates the venting instead of being on their side.

turns.ko: 몰라 적어도 10시 ㅋㅋㅋ 진짜 퇴사하고 싶다
turns.en: Dunno, at least 10pm lol I seriously wanna quit

turns.prompt: Sympathize and suggest a treat after work.

choices.en: You're really working so hard… how about chicken and beer after?
choices.feedback: 고생한다 + a fun plan (치맥) is the perfect friend move — comfort plus something to look forward to.

choices.en: You should decide on quitting carefully. (formal)
choices.feedback: Stiff lecture in 존댓말 — kills the mood when they just wanted to vent.

choices.en: 10pm? I'm already home though.
choices.feedback: Comes off as bragging and rubs in their bad situation.

turns.ko: 오 치맥 콜 ㅋㅋ 끝나면 톡할게
turns.en: Oh chicken and beer, deal lol I'll text you when I'm done

turns.prompt: Tell them to hang in there and you'll wait.

choices.en: Okay, hang in there! I'll be waiting
choices.feedback: 힘내 + 기다릴게 is a warm, natural casual send-off after a vent.

choices.en: Well then, keep up the good work. (formal)
choices.feedback: Very formal and distant; a close friend would naturally say 힘내 or 고생 많다.

choices.en: When's the report deadline again?
choices.feedback: Just repeats a question already answered — doesn't move the chat to a close.

title: Thinking about quitting a part-time job
situation: A friend texts that they're seriously considering quitting their part-time job because the manager is awful.
tip: When a friend is weighing a decision, react then dig with 되묻기 (왜?/무슨 일 있었어?) before giving any opinion — friends gather the story first.

turns.ko: 나 알바 그만둘까 진지하게 고민 중이야
turns.en: I'm seriously thinking about quitting my part-time job.

choices.en: What, out of nowhere? Did something happen?
choices.feedback: Reaction + 무슨 일 있었어? pulls the story out — the natural first response to a friend's big decision.

choices.en: You're planning to quit your part-time job? (formal)
choices.feedback: 그만두시려고요 is 존댓말, and 아르바이트 sounds textbook — friends say 알바 and 반말.

choices.en: Yeah good call, quit.
choices.feedback: Jumps to a verdict before hearing why — friends ask first.

turns.ko: 사장님이 자꾸 시간 막 바꾸고 어제는 괜히 나한테 짜증냄
turns.en: The boss keeps changing my hours randomly and yesterday he snapped at me for no reason

turns.prompt: Take their side and ask how long they've put up with it.

choices.ko: 헐 진짜 별로다… 그런 거 참은 지 얼마나 됐어?
choices.en: Ugh that's so lame… how long have you been putting up with that?
choices.feedback: Siding with them (별로다) + a follow-up keeps them talking and shows you're listening.

choices.en: The boss probably has his reasons too. (formal)
choices.feedback: Taking the boss's side in 존댓말 — the opposite of what a venting friend needs.

choices.en: How much do you get paid per hour?
choices.feedback: Random subject change to money — ignores the emotional point.

turns.ko: 한 세 달? 근데 막상 그만둔다 하니까 좀 무섭기도 하고
turns.en: Like three months? But now that I'm actually about to quit, it's kinda scary too

turns.prompt: Reassure them and gently nudge them to do what's best for them.

choices.ko: 그치 그 마음 이해돼. 그래도 너 힘들면 그만두는 게 맞지
choices.en: Yeah, I get that feeling. Still, if it's wearing you out, quitting is the right call
choices.feedback: 그치 (맞장구) + understanding + a gentle opinion — supportive without bulldozing.

choices.en: I hope you won't regret it. (formal)
choices.feedback: Cold 존댓말 send-off — sounds like a stranger, not a friend.

choices.en: Scared of what? Just keep working there.
choices.feedback: Brushes off their fear and contradicts them — not how a supportive friend reacts.

turns.ko: 고마워 ㅠㅠ 너랑 얘기하니까 마음 정리된다
turns.en: Thanks ㅠㅠ talking to you helps me sort my head out

choices.en: Tell me anytime lol let me know once you decide!
choices.feedback: Warm, open-ended, and asks to stay in the loop — a perfect friend close.

choices.en: I'm glad I could be of help. (formal)
choices.feedback: 다행입니다 is 존댓말 — too businesslike between close friends.

choices.ko: 그래서 결국 그만두는 거야 마는 거야?
choices.en: So are you quitting in the end or not?
choices.feedback: Pushy — pressures them for an answer right after they said they need to think.

title: Dreading a company dinner
situation: You two are hanging out when your friend groans about a forced company dinner (회식) they have to attend tonight.
tip: Face-to-face venting still runs on 맞장구 (헐/그니까) and 되묻기 (몇 차까지 가?) — match their energy out loud and keep the back-and-forth going.

turns.ko: 아 나 오늘 또 회식이야 가기 싫어 죽겠어
turns.en: Ugh, I've got another company dinner tonight, I so don't wanna go

turns.prompt: React and ask why the company dinners happen so often.

choices.ko: 또? 왜 이렇게 자주 해 ㅋㅋ
choices.en: Again? Why do you guys do it so often lol
choices.feedback: 또? (맞장구) + 왜 자주 해? bounces it back and matches their groan.

choices.en: Are you reluctant to attend the dinner? (formal)
choices.feedback: 참석하기 싫으신가요 is 존댓말 — bizarrely formal when sitting right next to a friend.

choices.en: Company dinners are part of work life.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a lecture — doesn't sympathize or keep the chat casual.

turns.ko: 팀장이 술을 너무 좋아해서 ㅋㅋ 맨날 2차 3차 가
turns.en: My team lead loves drinking lol we always go to a second and third round

turns.prompt: React to that and ask how late it usually runs.

choices.en: Whoa, up to a third round?? So what time does it end?
choices.feedback: Big reaction + 몇 시에 끝나? is genuine curiosity that keeps them venting.

choices.en: Drinking isn't good for your health. (formal)
choices.feedback: Preachy and in 존댓말 — totally kills a casual hangout vibe.

choices.en: I went to bed early yesterday though.
choices.feedback: Random and self-focused — ignores what they just said.

turns.ko: 기본 새벽 1시 ㅋㅋㅋ 진짜 집 가고 싶어
turns.en: Like 1am minimum lol I just wanna go home

turns.prompt: Sympathize hard and suggest a polite escape plan.

choices.ko: 와 그건 너무하다… 1차만 살짝 있다가 빠져!
choices.en: Wow that's too much… just stay for the first round and sneak out!
choices.feedback: 그건 너무하다 (empathy) + a practical tip is exactly the help a venting friend wants.

choices.en: Staying till the end is good manners. (formal)
choices.feedback: Formal etiquette lecture — the last thing they want to hear right now.

choices.en: 1am means the last train's already gone, take a taxi.
choices.feedback: Fixates on a logistics detail and skips the emotional support.

turns.en: I should do that lol I'll drink a bit and bail

turns.prompt: Cheer them on and tell them to text you after.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그래 적당히 해! 끝나고 톡해
choices.en: Lol yeah, take it easy! Text me when it's over
choices.feedback: Light encouragement + 끝나고 톡해 wraps the hangout chat naturally.

choices.en: I hope you have a pleasant time. (formal)
choices.feedback: 존댓말 well-wishing sounds like a card, not a friend.

choices.en: Wait, why don't you wanna go to the dinner again?
choices.feedback: Re-asks something already explained — stalls instead of closing the chat.
